# harborpilot_budget (Resource)

A spending limit for a scope, per calendar period or one time (never resets), enforced in the reservation path.

Changes made outside Terraform are detected on refresh and shown as a diff of `spec`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "harborpilot_budget" "checkout" {
  name = "checkout-monthly"
  spec = jsonencode({
    scope       = "project"
    scope_id    = harborpilot_project.checkout.id
    period      = "month"
    limit       = "200"
    currency    = "USD"
    enforcement = "block"
    warn_at     = 0.8
    enabled     = true
  })
}

# A one-time budget: a total limit that never resets. Spend counts from the
# budget's creation unless starts_at is set; ends_at is optional. Leave
# timezone out. Needs Harbor Pilot 0.1.4 or later.
resource "harborpilot_budget" "trial_credit" {
  name = "trial-credit"
  spec = jsonencode({
    scope    = "project"
    scope_id = harborpilot_project.checkout.id
    period   = "once"
    limit    = "50"
    currency = "USD"
    ends_at  = "2027-06-30T23:59:59Z"
    enabled  = true
  })
}
```

## One-time budgets

A budget with `period = "once"` is a total limit that never resets. They need Harbor Pilot 0.1.4 or later: an older server rejects `period = "once"` with a 422 validation error.

- `starts_at` and `ends_at` are optional RFC 3339 times. They apply only to one-time budgets; a recurring budget rejects them.
- An empty `starts_at` means "from the budget's creation". Replacing the resource (`terraform apply -replace`, or removing it and adding it back) creates a new budget, so the window starts again and earlier spend no longer counts. Set `starts_at` to keep a fixed window.
- **Start over** in the Harbor Pilot UI (or `POST /api/v1/budgets/{id}/reset`) sets `starts_at` to the current time. Terraform shows this as drift on `starts_at` in `spec`: apply to restore your configuration, or copy the new `starts_at` into it to keep the restart.
- Leave `timezone` out (or empty) for one-time budgets; it only sets period boundaries for `day`, `week` and `month`.

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name (lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`).
- `spec` (String) The budget specification as JSON, usually written with `jsonencode({...})`. See the `BudgetSpec` schema in the Harbor Pilot API reference. Properties you leave out take their zero value (empty string, list or map, `0`, `false`), except `enabled`, which must be set.

### Read-Only

- `drift_state` (String) `drifted` when the object was changed outside Terraform since Terraform last wrote it.
- `id` (String) Stable object id.
- `managed_by` (String) Source of the last change (`terraform` after an apply).
- `revision` (Number) Server revision, used for optimistic concurrency.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by id or by name.
terraform import harborpilot_budget.example <id-or-name>
```
